why: Coverage code-references RETIRED from the live manifests after R-B.
A coverage claim can be deleted, or an ambiguous historical pointer can
be superseded by qualified concrete surfaces. The R6 -> R7 ledgers record
RENAMES and assert that R-B 'moved paths, it did not add, drop or merge an
owner'. Either later event must be recorded here rather than by rewriting
a ledger in place, which those files forbid.
This file is the third term that keeps R6's total of 313 PROVABLE rather
than edited: every reference R7 names is either live in a manifest today
or retired here, with the authority that retired it. A silent edit to a
ledger still fails; a deliberate retirement is recorded and passes.

reason: NECB 2020 contains neither Article 8.4.2.12 nor Sentence 8.4.2.2.(6).
Verified against the official NRC NECB 2020 second printing including
the 2025-02-27 errata: Division B page 8-3 gives Article 8.4.2.2
Sentences (1) to (5) only, and page 8-5 makes 8.4.2.10 the last
article of Subsection 8.4.2. The HBIX 2020-to-2025 Part 8 comparison
So this coverage row described a provision that edition does not have.
Sol ruled it DELETED rather than mapped onto the Code's general
alternative-solution framework, because an alternative solution and
the 2025 exceptional-calculation method are not the same requirement.
The 2025 claim for 8.4.2.12 is untouched: it exists there.
The unqualified symbol resolves to three methods: Backend.execute,
Local.execute and Remote.execute. The generated AHJ-facing document
selected the first and linked both editions to Backend.execute's
Both coverage rows now name Local.execute and Remote.execute
explicitly. The historical ledger remains unchanged; the two
qualified surfaces are recorded in the additions ledger.
